svg.title: The Markdown preview — okfy algorithm explainer
svg.desc: How a concept's Markdown becomes the preview without a library. One pass: markdownInput bounds the raw text to 512 KiB of characters and replaces control characters with U+FFFD instead of deleting them, so they can never join two pieces of syntax into one. renderMarkdown normalises the line endings and splits the text into lines. writeMarkdownBlocks then makes a single pass, collecting the footnote definitions and tracking fences and code spans so that a footnote-looking line inside a fence stays literal, and writing each block: heading, paragraph, list, blockquote, table, fenced code and horizontal rule. writeMarkdownInline scans the inline text of every block. Every leaf is escaped where it is written, and the parts are joined into one HTML string, so nothing is parsed twice. The inline scanner turns code into code elements with the text escaped, a link into an anchor where an https, http or mailto URL opens in a new tab, an image into an img element carrying alt and a data-embed marker with no source yet, a footnote reference into a reference, and one to three emphasis markers into strong, em and del. A newline in a paragraph becomes a line break, and a list item continues on a line indented past its marker. A backslash escape gives a literal character, the wiki forms resolve inside the bundle, and a footnote definition that is nothing but a URL is left out of the footnote list and shown as an inline external-link marker at its reference. Escaping happens at the sink: text leaves through esc, which turns ampersand, less-than, greater-than and the double quote into entities, and an attribute value leaves through markdownAttr, which escapes the single quote as well. So an image tag written into a concept reaches the page as the words a reader sees, and generated HTML is never parsed again and never substituted into an attribute, so a bundle cannot create an event handler. A link's target is accepted only for http, https and mailto, with no credentials and no control characters or backslashes. Images are written first and sourced later: the renderer writes an img element with alt and a data-embed marker, and hydratePreviewImages resolves each embed against the bundle, validates the URL, and only then sets the source through the DOM. An embed that does not resolve is replaced with its alt text, external, data and raw blob images are never shown, and at most 64 images are loaded per preview, four at a time, eight mebibytes each and sixteen mebibytes in total. One shared budget bounds the input at 512 KiB, the output at 2 MiB, the nesting at 24 levels and the search work at 32 times the input, and exceeding any of the four throws the same limit, so the whole preview is replaced with the notice "Markdown preview omitted: safety limit exceeded" rather than a partial render.
svg.text: Raw syntax in, escaped text out, and one budget over the whole render
The input is bounded first: at most 512 KiB of characters, and control characters become U+FFFD
instead of being deleted, so they cannot join two pieces of syntax into one.
The block pass tracks fences and code spans, so a line that looks like a footnote inside a fence stays
literal. Each block is written once, straight to escaped text, so nothing is ever parsed twice.
What the scanner makes of each token
<code> with the text escaped; a fence becomes <pre><code>
an <a>; an https, http or mailto URL opens in a new tab
an with alt and data-embed, and no src yet
a footnote reference; a URL-only definition shows ↗ here instead
, and a list item continues on a line indented past its marker
A backslash escape gives a literal character, and the wiki forms [[page]] and ![[image]] resolve inside the
bundle. Emphasis takes one to three markers, and a table row splits on pipes outside code and links.
Every leaf is escaped where it is written
the last only in an attribute value
the tag reaches the page as the words a reader sees, and never as markup
Text leaves through esc(); an attribute value leaves through markdownAttr(), which also escapes the quote.
Output is never parsed again and never put into an attribute, so a bundle cannot create an event handler.
An image is written first and sourced later
then, once the URL is validated
The embed is resolved against the bundle and its URL is checked first; only then is the source set, through the DOM.
An embed that does not resolve is replaced by its alt text. External, data: and raw blob: images are never shown.
At most 64 images in one preview, fetched 4 at a time, 8 MiB each and 16 MiB in total.
By the time the tag has a source, the source has been checked, so a hostile src never reaches the markup.
Markdown preview omitted: safety limit exceeded.
Exceeding any bound throws the same shared limit, so the whole preview is replaced with this notice
rather than a partial render, and a pathological concept can never hang the preview.
It is deliberately a bounded renderer, not a full CommonMark implementation: pathological input gets the notice.
The renderer is the only thing that writes markup, so nothing a bundle says is ever executed.
